evals.prompt:
Checkout form's submit control is `
Place order
` inside a `
`. Keyboard users report Enter does nothing on the control, and double orders happen while pending because aria-disabled does not stop the click handler. Review and give the smallest safe fix.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the missing native button contract (no implicit submit, no Enter/Space activation, no real disabled state), proposes `<button type="submit" disabled={pending}>` as the smallest structural change, and routes the rendered role/state/keyboard regression test to a11y-contract-testing.
expectations: The response names the specific native contracts a div cannot provide: implicit submit behavior inside a form, Enter and Space activation, and a real disabled state that blocks click dispatch.
It states that aria-disabled only reports state to assistive technology and does not prevent the onClick handler from firing, unlike the native disabled attribute.
The fix is the native element swap to `<button type="submit">` rather than adding role="button" plus keydown handlers on the div.
The rendered role, name, state, and keyboard-path regression test is routed to a11y-contract-testing rather than written as part of this skill's finding.

evals.prompt: A teammate files this under semantic-markup-contracts: "axe reports no violations but our `getByRole('button', { name: 'Filter' })` query fails and Tab order in the toolbar is wrong. Please add role and accessible-name assertions plus a full keyboard-navigation suite for the toolbar." The toolbar is built from real `<button>` elements wrapped in a `<div role="toolbar">`.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the routing: with native buttons already in place there is no element-choice defect, and writing rendered role/name/state and keyboard-path tests is a11y-contract-testing's scope. States what evidence would move it back into this skill and hands the test work over.
expectations: The response declines to own the request as filed, because the markup already uses the native element whose implicit role matches the action.
It states that adding redundant ARIA to elements with the correct implicit role is not the fix and can create duplicate or worse semantics.
It names the evidence that would change the verdict: rendered DOM showing a clickable div/span, a link with href="#" used as a command, or interactive elements nested inside each other.
Authoring the getByRole, accessible-name, and Tab-order assertions is routed to a11y-contract-testing.

evals.prompt: Every card in a search-results grid renders its title as `<h1 className="text-sm">` because the designer wanted the type token reused. A reviewer says this is fine for screen readers since the HTML outline algorithm re-ranks nested headings by section depth, and separately says the page will be penalized in search because there are 20 h1 elements.
evals.expected_output: Corrects the outline-algorithm premise, confirms the flat h1 repetition is a real structure defect for assistive technology and heading-based tests, downgrades the SEO framing to a soft signal, and gives a small rank fix that keeps the visual size.
expectations: The response states the HTML outline algorithm was never implemented by browsers or assistive technology and was removed from the HTML spec, so nesting does not re-rank headings.
It concludes that structure comes from the literal h1 to h6 rank in logical document order, so 20 sibling h1 elements flatten the page's section structure.
The fix keeps the visual type token and changes only the rank, for example an h2 or h3 per card under the results-section heading, rather than restyling or removing the headings.
The SEO claim is stated as a soft structure signal rather than a ranking penalty, since the title text is still indexed.

evals.prompt: Following your earlier review we replaced the div-with-onClick submit control with `<button type="submit">` inside the existing `<form>`. Now the form performs a real native submit, the browser blocks it on a `required` email field and shows its own bubble, and our custom inline error component never renders. Roll the button back to a div so our JS validation keeps working.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the rollback, explains that the blocking condition is the now-active native validity lifecycle rather than the element choice, keeps the native button, and routes the novalidate / setCustomValidity / reportValidity design to constraint-validation-contracts.
expectations: The response keeps the native button and rejects reverting to a div, since the div would reintroduce the missing keyboard, disabled, and submit contracts.
It explains that the new symptom is the native constraint-validation lifecycle becoming reachable for the first time, not a defect introduced by the semantic fix.
It identifies the concrete decision point as whether the form opts out with novalidate and drives messaging in JS, or keeps native validation and styles it, without designing that lifecycle here.
The validity-lifecycle work, including reportValidity, setCustomValidity, and the :invalid styling contract, is routed to constraint-validation-contracts.
Any follow-up test asserting the rendered error is announced and associated is routed to a11y-contract-testing.
